Scaling inference-at-deployment lowers the number of simultaneously served copies of each new model. For example, if inference-at-deployment is scaled by two orders of magnitude, the number of copies can decrease by a factor of 100, meaning the new model can only be immediately deployed in 1% as many tasks as it would be if it had been scaled by pre-training compute. 

Additionally, scaling inference-at-deployment reduces the value of securing model weights. If training compute plateaus at a certain level while inference-at-deployment scales significantly, the value of stealing model weights does not increase over time, as the costs associated with inference-at-deployment would be much higher than the training costs of the model that was stolen.
